A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TianQuan-S2S study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original ERA5 forecasting experiments, deterministic and ensemble comparisons, and ablations in Figure 3, Tables 1–3, and the appendices.

after.justification: V5 retains those original experiments and reports additional fusion, perturbation, continuity, regional, and heatwave results.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the specified fusion-attention normalization from sqrt(D) to sqrt(N), where N = H×W. The climatology fusion, noisy Transformer, loss, and multi-model forecasting strategy otherwise remain. Additional temporal-embedding details do not establish a newly introduced component.

E1.justification: The ERA5 dataset, meteorological variables, and global forecasting task remain. V5 adds targeted North American and East Asian evaluations, particularly two 2018 heatwave scenarios in Appendix H, extending the evaluated conditions within the existing data.

E2.justification: The external benchmark baselines remain, including XGBoost and Lasso already evaluated in v4 Table 11. V5 Table 4 adds explicit fusion and perturbation alternatives: Concat, Gate, initial-condition perturbations, and fixed nonlearnable noise.

E3.justification: V5 substantially expands the evaluation design with controlled fusion, noise-location and noise-scale comparisons, first-order output-difference measurements, and 25/40-day heatwave checks. Section 4 also rewrites TianQuan ensemble generation around block-level noise, although retained initial-state wording leaves ambiguity. The 51-member count, data splits, resolutions, and training budget remain unchanged; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: V5 adds detailed fusion and perturbation controls, noise-depth/scale sensitivity, temporal-continuity analysis, regional and additional-variable ablations, and heatwave cases. It removes v4's daily-versus-five-day comparison and layer-to-lead-time alignment study (Tables 8–9). The autoregressive-versus-multi-model comparison is retained as v5 Table 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V5 Table 9's standard deviations describe differences between forecast outputs for continuity analysis, not uncertainty in estimated performance. Ensemble size and probabilistic scoring practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3, the retained forecasting-strategy comparison, Table 11, and existing forecast plots retain their results. V5 adds substantial diagnostic and regional results while removing v4 Tables 8–9. For example, new Table 14 reports 25-day North American heatwave RMSE of 2.522 for TianQuan-S2S, 2.634 for FuXi-S2S, and 2.948 for ClimaX; these are new scenario results, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of fusion-attention weights changes its scaling dimension from D to N in Section 3.1, beyond a typesetting change. Equation 1 also corrects inconsistent time indices to match the already-described history and forecast horizon. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: climatology-aware embeddings and an uncertainty-augmented Transformer mitigate oversmoothing and improve S2S forecasting against numerical and data-driven baselines. The additional evidence does not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: V5 adds substantive explanations of temporal continuity, fusion and perturbation choices, and Wind10 difficulties arising from missing detailed surface and radiation inputs. Appendix H qualifies performance on extreme events. It also removes v4's layer-to-lead-time interpretation and discussion of the accuracy–cost tradeoff behind five-day intervals.

D1.justification: V5 adds a code-repository pointer and a reproducibility statement advertising README instructions for data preparation and execution. It newly specifies lead-time/absolute-time embeddings and the climatology baseline's 61-day window. Core hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged; repository contents are outside the supplied evidence.

R1.justification: V5 adds Buizza et al. (2005) to motivate perturbations and Zheng et al. (2025) in related work, expands S2S citations, and removes Bonavita (2023). Its principal positioning relative to FuXi-S2S and other forecasting models remains.

P1.justification: Most core prose and section order are retained. V5 makes local wording and terminology corrections, expands explanations, adds acknowledgments, reproducibility and LLM-use disclosures, and introduces an appendix Discussion section. Author affiliations and publication-header text also change.

P2.justification: V5 substantially expands diagnostic displays with fusion/perturbation, continuity, regional, heatwave, and noise-scale tables plus Figure 6's heatmaps, while removing two earlier analysis tables. Existing figures are resized, relocated, or relabeled; Figure 3 gains variable headings. The document also adopts ICLR formatting.

improvement.justification: The added mechanism controls, heatwave checks, code-access information, and explicit Wind10 limitations modestly strengthen support and transparency. Gains are tempered by removed diagnostics, ambiguous ensemble wording, and new reporting inconsistencies: Table 4 gives day-45 FLN RMSE as 2.617, while Table 15's sigma=1 fixed-noise row gives 2.719 without explaining the difference. These limitations prevent a substantial overall improvement.
